issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the image class in the example program: the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) declares the class as 'Image24' while its constructors are named 'Bitmap24' and the implementation file (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines/implements 'Bitmap24::Bitmap24'. The solution header (solution_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) consistently declares 'Bitmap24'. This mismatch (header class name != constructor/implementation name) will cause compile-time errors and confusion for students (the header's class identifier does not match the implementation nor the intended solution).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template header to match the implementation and solution. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'class Image24' to 'class Bitmap24' so the header's class name, its constructors, the .cpp implementation, and the solution all use the same identifier. This preserves the intended API and allows the project to compile.

issues.description: The header file template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares the class as 'Image24' (class Image24) while the implementation file template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp defines/uses 'Bitmap24' (constructors/destructor and methods). The solution repository uses the class name 'Bitmap24' in both header and implementation. This mismatch means the header's declared type name does not match the implementation and the reference solution: students editing or compiling the template will see constructor/destructor declarations named 'Bitmap24' inside a class named 'Image24', causing confusion and compilation errors (no clear mapping from the header to the .cpp and solution).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template header (template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) from 'Image24' to 'Bitmap24' so the class name matches the filename, the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp), and the solution. Ensure the constructor and destructor declarations inside the header are 'Bitmap24()' and '~Bitmap24()' and that all references in the template use 'Bitmap24'. This preserves the intended API and removes the compilation/mapping mismatch.
